title: Scouting's Real Crisis Is Not Marketing. It Is Decades of Neglect.
summary: This article argues that the Boy Scouts of America's declining membership and reputation problems stem from decades of institutional neglect and internal dysfunction, not merely ineffective marketing campaigns. The author suggests that structural problems, leadership failures, and outdated practices have eroded trust over generations, making surface-level rebranding insufficient.
problem_solved: Diagnoses why traditional scouting organizations are struggling to retain members and relevance in modern society.
why_valuable: Challenges surface-level explanations and argues for understanding deep-rooted organizational pathology rather than symptoms.
